chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him)
That he used to break the mihrabs when he saw them in the mosques, and he would say, 'They are like the slaughterhouses of the Jews.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali break the mihrabs in mosques?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) would break the mihrabs found in mosques, comparing them to the slaughterhouses of the Jews, indicating a specific jurisprudential or theological view on their form or function. This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia scholarly debate regarding whether the mihrab is a bid'ah (innovation) or a permissible sunnah, with early Imams often critiquing its architectural prominence as a distraction from the unity of prayer space. The comparison to Jewish slaughterhouses suggests a view that the mihrab may have been adopted from pre-Islamic or Jewish architectural practices, potentially introducing an element of ritualism or physical division into the mosque.
